assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed-data margin induced by \(P\).

standard.name: Known uniform-design specialization of the pointwise Hölder model

novel.justification: The condition describes observational problems in which treatment selection and baseline prognosis vary more sharply than the treatment effect, including smooth effect-modification models with rough clinical assignment and risk surfaces. It ensures that a macro effect neighborhood contains asymptotically many nuisance microcells.

This is the nondegenerate central-privacy range in which a bounded scalar release can carry information; it includes every fixed privacy budget and privacy budgets shrinking no faster than the reciprocal sample size.

definitions.name: Exact-uniform full unknown-propensity Hölder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_H=\{P:P\text{ is a law on }(X,A,Y_0,Y_1,Y)\text{ inducing }O\in\mathcal O\text{ and satisfying }\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:exchangeability},\text{ass:uniform-design},\text{ass:overlap},\text{ass:propensity-holder},\text{ass:control-holder},\text{ass:effect-holder},\text{ass:two-scale-regime}\}\), indexed by \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,q,L,e_0,x_0\).

definitions.name: Pure-private minimax absolute risk
definitions.construction: \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}=\inf_{T_{\mathrm{DP}}:\,\epsilon\text{-DP}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n},T_{\mathrm{DP}}}|T_{\mathrm{DP}}(D_n)-\theta(P)|\), where privacy holds on every pair \(D_n\sim_1D_n'\).

definitions.name: Occupancy-weighted second-order score
definitions.construction: Partition the side-\(h\) cube around \(x_0\) into \(k\asymp h^d/\ell^d\) public cells \(C_j\) of mass \(v\asymp\ell^d\). For a bounded symmetric kernel \(Z_{\mathrm{pair}}\), form the within-cell ordered-pair average \(B_j\) and set \(S_{\mathrm{occ}}=\sum_{j=1}^kN_jB_j\), with \(B_j=0\) if \(N_j<2\).

definitions.name: Ordered target-shell selector
definitions.construction: At resolution \(r\), use \(t_P\) and \(\mathcal S_m(P;r)\) on \(\mathcal G_r\), define \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\) as displayed in the symbol table, and release \(T_{\mathrm{shell}}\) with conditional probabilities proportional to \(\exp\{-\epsilon Q_t(D_n)/2\}\).

definitions.name: Occupancy-weighted full-fiber projection handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(H_{\mathrm{occ}}\) at \(r=\rho_\star\): solve finite two-fiber minimax tests on nested Hölder sieves; extract each test's first nonzero localized Hoeffding projection; replace an unnormalized all-pairs sum by \(S_{\mathrm{occ}}\); clip record projections at their public concentration envelope; rescale each target score to replacement sensitivity one; and pass the resulting \(Q_t\) to the ordered target-shell selector.

definitions.name: One-shot adaptive occupancy handle
definitions.construction: Apply \(H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\): release one correlated multiscale array of occupancy-weighted projection scores and use only post-processing to perform Lepski comparisons over \(\Theta_{\mathrm{sm}}\), while retaining the ordered target-shell aggregation of \(H_{\mathrm{occ}}\).

statements.statement: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and overlap, \(\mu_a(x)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X=x]\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\). Hölder continuity makes \(\tau\) the unique continuous representative of \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), so \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\) is identified.
statements.justification: The continuous-version convention makes a pointwise causal effect well defined at a covariate value having probability zero.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. use the same identifying assumptions; this lemma records the representative needed by the private pointwise problem.
statements.consumer: It gives the private risk a causal rather than merely regression-functional interpretation.

statements.statement: Suppose \(Z_{\mathrm{pair}}\in[-1,1]\) is symmetric and \(\mathbb E_P[Z_{\mathrm{pair}}(O_1,O_2)\mid X_1,X_2\in C_j]=\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) for every \(j\). Then \[\mathbb E_PS_{\mathrm{occ}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}knv\{1-(1-v)^{n-1}\}.\] Moreover, \(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|S_{\mathrm{occ}}(D_n)-S_{\mathrm{occ}}(D_n')|\le12\). Consequently the usable private signal is of order \(\epsilon|\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}|n h^d\min\{1,n\ell^d\}\), uniformly from \(n\ell^d\ll1\) to \(n\ell^d\gg1\).
statements.justification: Multiplying a cell average by its realized occupancy converts pair collisions into linear dense-cell information without increasing global sensitivity with occupancy.
statements.gap: The banked sparse score weights each usable cell equally, while Zeng et al. condition on all realized cell counts and Chaudhuri et al. control local projections; the displayed identity is the missing causal sparse-to-dense interpolation.
statements.consumer: It supplies the sensitivity and signal calculation needed for full-class target-fiber tests at every cell occupancy.

statements.statement: If every \(Q_t\) has replacement sensitivity at most one and \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le B_{\mathrm{shell}}\), then \(T_{\mathrm{shell}}\) is pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private and \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|T_{\mathrm{shell}}-\theta(P)|\le(B_{\mathrm{shell}}+3)r.\] The constant does not depend on \(|\mathcal G_r|\) or on a nuisance-sieve cardinality.
statements.justification: The weighted-shell functional turns scalar ordering into a log-free risk certificate for the exponential selector.
statements.gap: Asi et al.'s general T-mechanism controls a finite cover through global counting; this proposition isolates a stronger ordered-fiber certificate without asserting that arbitrary models satisfy it.
statements.consumer: Any successful construction of the full-fiber scores immediately yields a finite pure-private pointwise-CATE estimator.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{lower}}>0\), depending only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that throughout \(n\epsilon\ge1\), \[R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\}.\] The \(\rho_G\) term is witnessed by a localized one-record subexperiment. The \(\rho_F\) term is witnessed inside \(\mathcal M_H\) by smooth shared-sign two-fiber mixtures whose expected Hamming transport changes from order \(n^2h^d\ell^d\) to order \(nh^d\) across \(n\ell^d\asymp1\).
statements.justification: A same-class converse determines whether dense occupancy creates a new privacy radius or merely activates the first-order branch.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. give only the nonprivate term, and Acharya et al. give generic coupling inequalities rather than the occupancy-indexed causal mixtures needed for the two privacy terms.
statements.consumer: It prevents an upper mechanism from being certified against a surrogate regression class or only a sparse diagnostic family.

statements.statement: For \(r=C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star\), can \(H_{\mathrm{occ}}\) construct one finite family \(\{Q_t:t\in\mathcal G_r\}\) on the full class \(\mathcal M_H\) such that \(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|Q_t(D_n)-Q_t(D_n')|\le1\) for every \(t\), \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C_{\mathrm{shell}}\), and \(C_{\mathrm{shell}}\) is independent of the Hölder-sieve dimension, uniformly over all values of \(n\ell^d\)?
statements.justification: This is the genuine construction problem: the occupancy identity must survive profiling over every unknown propensity and outcome-regression nuisance without an entropy payment.
statements.gap: The downgraded parent reaches only a sparse shared-sign family, while Asi et al. and Chaudhuri et al. do not provide nuisance-independent composite CATE fiber scores.
statements.consumer: An affirmative answer combines with the shell proposition and the same-class lower bound to settle the pure-private pointwise-CATE frontier.

statements.statement: If Open-ended Question 1 has an affirmative answer, the resulting finite selector satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|T_{\mathrm{shell}}-\theta(P)|\le C_{\mathrm{upper}}\rho_\star,\qquad R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.\] This strictly extends the nonprivate frontier of Kennedy et al. on the exact-uniform two-scale subclass by identifying and attaining both pure-privacy branches, and it holds without a nuisance-sieve logarithm.
statements.justification: The theorem is the matched sparse-to-dense minimax statement and makes the privacy elbows the paper's named focal object.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. establish the nonprivate pointwise rate, and Schröder et al. establish approximate-private releases; neither gives a pure-private minimax law over the full unknown-propensity Hölder class.
statements.consumer: Researchers releasing individualized treatment effects obtain a principled resolution and privacy calibration rather than a learner-specific noise heuristic.

statements.statement: For fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1]\) and \(q<\gamma\), both \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_F\) are no larger in order than \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\). Hence Theorem 2 reduces to \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), the Kennedy et al. pointwise-CATE frontier, whenever privacy does not shrink with \(n\).
statements.justification: The required special-case reduction checks that privacy does not spuriously degrade the classical fixed-budget asymptotics.
statements.gap: This reduction is a consistency check against Kennedy et al., not a separate novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It lets applied users recover the established nonprivate benchmark in regimes where privacy is asymptotically free.

statements.statement: Can \(H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) produce one pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private estimator, without knowing \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\Theta_{\mathrm{sm}}\), whose risk is within the smallest possible logarithmic factor of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) simultaneously across sparse and dense occupancy, and can a matching adaptive lower bound determine that factor?
statements.justification: Unknown smoothness is the first deployment-level uncertainty after the fixed-class frontier is settled, and privacy may make its penalty regime dependent.
statements.gap: Cai et al. characterize adaptation for federated density estimation, while Kennedy et al. leave nonprivate CATE adaptation open; no result combines nuisance elbows, occupancy, and pure central privacy.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether one private release can be tuned for individualized-effect analysis without disclosing or prespecifying smoothness.

sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary observational treatment with unknown Hölder propensity \(\pi\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The proposed target-fiber mechanism profiles over the full propensity and control-regression Hölder classes; no named nuisance estimator and no fixed finite nuisance sieve is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 establish the nonprivate pointwise Hölder-CATE minimax rate, with the upper construction in Section 5.
Section 4 uses treated--control occupancy and effect homogeneity to obtain a global nonprivate rate with a collision term.
The paper stabilizes central-private U-statistics using local Hájek projections and tuple reweighting.
Section 4 gives a general pure-private T-mechanism based on clipped likelihood-ratio tests and finite covers.
The paper gives central-private Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad inequalities based on expected Hamming transport.
Theorems 1 and 3 give finite-query and functional observational CATE releases under approximate differential privacy.
The sparse-histogram lower bound and compact dense-histogram theorem show that pure-private costs can change with representation and occupancy.
Theorems 1--2 and the adaptive lower bound characterize extra logarithmic costs for pointwise federated-private density adaptation.
The paper establishes nonprivate heterogeneous-effect minimax rates with explicit random-design geometry.
Definition 2 and Section 4 construct T-estimators from coherent tests on countable model nets.

tldr: Pointwise CATE estimation over the unknown-propensity Hölder model has a nonprivate nuisance-smoothness elbow, while pure privacy creates a second transition governed by observations per localization cell. The proposed occupancy-weighted pair score has constant replacement sensitivity and signal proportional to \(n h^d\min\{1,n\ell^d\}\), so its sparse collision branch and dense first-order branch meet at \(n\ell^d\asymp1\). The central open step is to lift this identity from signed diagnostic mixtures to all target fibers without paying nuisance-sieve entropy. An affirmative lift yields the matched full-class frontier \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\).

project_justification.gap: No located result gives a pure-central-DP minimax frontier for pointwise CATE with unknown smooth propensity and outcome regression. The closest banked construction uses only exactly-two-record cells and therefore loses all signal when cell occupancy diverges.
project_justification.niche: Realized cell occupancy can amplify a degenerate nuisance-product signal while preserving constant record influence, potentially joining the sparse \(n^2\epsilon\) branch to the dense \(n\epsilon\) branch with no third radius.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates the exact occupancy identity, derives a same-class lower frontier, and reduces full-class attainment to a nuisance-independent weighted-shell certificate for occupancy-weighted Hoeffding projections.

related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman derive the nonprivate Hölder pointwise-CATE frontier and a localized higher-order R-learner; the present target adds pure-private sparse and dense branches on its exact-uniform two-scale specialization. Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy supply the conditioning-on-counts idea for a global discrete-covariate causal estimator, but do not privatize localized nuisance-product projections. Chaudhuri, Loh, Pandey, and Sarkar stabilize private U-statistics through local Hájek projections; their generic kernel theory informs the sensitivity step rather than establishing a CATE fiber theorem. Birgé's Definition 2 supplies the coherent-test architecture for scalar target fibers. Asi, Duchi, Haque, Li, and Ruan convert stable tests into pure-private estimators, but their general cover analysis does not furnish entropy-free full CATE-fiber scores. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang provide the Hamming-coupling converse used to certify both privacy branches. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel release orthogonal CATE queries with Gaussian perturbations under approximate privacy, a distinct privacy model without a minimax Hölder frontier. Balcer and Vadhan show why sparse and dense pure-private representations can obey different error laws. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen provide the one-shot multiscale and adaptive-lower-bound templates for the follow-on adaptation question. Gao and Han clarify why random-design geometry can change heterogeneous-effect rates, but their model and estimators are nonprivate.
technical_internal_limitation: The identity in Lemma 2 does not itself solve the full-fiber problem. For arbitrary least-favorable priors, the second-order kernel orientation can depend on a growing nuisance profile, and clipping local projections can reintroduce a sieve-size factor. The proposed early kill test is the finite \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\) two-resolution program from the parent archive: impose every replacement-neighbor constraint, increase both occupancy and nuisance-sign dimension, and reject the route if the optimized weighted-shell functional grows with the nuisance dimension after occupancy weighting.
honest_scope: The fixed-smoothness exact-uniform model is the primary scope. The occupancy-amplification lemma and same-class lower bound are theorem claims; the nuisance-independent full-fiber score is deliberately exposed as Open-ended Question 1, and the combined upper frontier is conditional on its resolution. Transfer to a merely bounded known design density is not claimed. For fixed \(\epsilon\) and \(q<\gamma\), the proposed frontier reduces to the published nonprivate pointwise-CATE order. Smoothness adaptation is a separate open question rather than part of the fixed-class headline.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the parent's indicator of exactly two records by \(N_jB_j\), prove constant replacement sensitivity, and then establish a nuisance-independent weighted-shell bound.

literature_map: The selected kernel is anchored to Kennedy et al.'s Theorems 1--2 and Section 5, which fix the pointwise Hölder-CATE class, the nonprivate elbow, and the localized higher-order proof architecture. Zeng et al.'s Section 4 supplies the occupancy-conditioned treated--control construction showing that cells with more than two records should be weighted rather than discarded. Chaudhuri et al.'s local Hájek-projection algorithm and sensitivity proof supply the record-influence stabilization move for second-order scores. Asi et al.'s Section 4 T-mechanism supplies clipped stable testing and exponential selection, while the proposed ordered-shell functional replaces its global cover count. Acharya et al.'s private Le Cam and Assouad coupling arguments supply the same-class converse. Searches of pure-private pointwise CATE, occupancy-normalized causal U-statistics, and full-function private CATE found only Niu et al. and Schröder et al.; these provide general or approximate-private releases, not the target minimax frontier. Balcer and Vadhan establish a structurally analogous sparse--dense representation divide for histograms, not causal projection scores. No closer paper was found that subsumes the occupancy-weighted full-fiber kernel.
novelty_justification: The closest theorem-level result is Kennedy et al.'s nonprivate pointwise-CATE frontier; the strict delta is a pure-private two-branch frontier on its exact-uniform two-scale subclass together with an attaining finite mechanism. The closest privacy result for CATE is Schröder et al.'s Gaussian approximate-private release, which neither treats pure privacy nor derives a minimax rate. The closest method result is Chaudhuri et al.'s private U-statistic stabilization, which addresses a fixed kernel rather than composite target fibers with unknown causal nuisances. The occupancy identity makes the dense transition auditable, while the proposal keeps the remaining full-fiber entropy cancellation visible as its central open question.
message: Authored and structurally validated the occupancy-weighted full-class sparse-to-dense pure-DP pointwise-CATE frontier core.
